choices.A: Treat them as exact values for the entire population
choices.B: Use them as estimates and explain how the sample was selected
choices.C: The sample size is no longer needed
choices.D: The data can be changed to make the conclusions look better

question: How should conclusions drawn from a sample in a case study be used?
solution: A statistical case study should report both the source of the data and the limitations of its conclusions. A sample includes only part of the population, so population conclusions drawn from it should be treated as estimates. The sampling method affects how well the sample represents the population, so it should be explained. Therefore, choose B.
